nature: EXPLORATORY follow-up of the formal experiment (experiment.json). Four alternative ways to compare segmented rule lists with the global list. The motivating lead (F6 beats G at budget 20 on Validation) was found on Validation, so Validation results here are DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. A confirmatory-style check is only possible on Test, which requires a separate explicit user decision and a committed configs/future_B/FREEZE.json.
known_information_before_registration: all results of experiment.json on Discovery/Validation (docs section 11), in particular: E9 Validation F6 - G = +4.03 pp at B=20 (R1 p=0.030), +0.02 at B=50, -0.88 at B=100; F ties G at all budgets

per-group E9 Validation coverage of F and F6 own lists vs G's list at B=20 and B=100 (computed descriptively on 2026-11-22): F6 group 2-0 (74 customers) G covers 47% at B=100, own list +6.5 pp at B=20
Validation coverage by order size: 1-5 items ~24%, 6-15 ~81%, 16-30 ~98%, 31+ ~100%
D: future mean confidence of deployed rules G 0.532 vs RFM L 0.527 (Test, RFM groups)
nothing was computed for budgets 5 or 10, for the leave-one-out metric, for worst-group gains of random controls, or for revenue weighting

frozen_inputs.controls: regenerated exactly as experiment.json: F -> S, A1, B1, B2; F6 -> S, A1, R1; seeds 1000-1099
frozen_inputs.rules: P5 (configs/extra_eval/common.json), Discovery counts, E9 per-group lists with E10 V3 combination de-duplication (extra_eval.e9.build)
frozen_inputs.systems: G, L (RFM, reference only), F, F6 and all control seeds

main_target: F6 (the lead). F is reported alongside with its controls; L is a reference without controls.

C1_small_budget_curve.question: With only a few recommendation slots, are segmented lists better than the global list?
C1_small_budget_curve.metric: E9 order coverage (restricted: each customer uses own group's list of B combinations) at every budget; summary = mean coverage over the small budgets 5, 10, 20
C1_small_budget_curve.primary: H1: F6 small-budget mean minus G, paired customer bootstrap (2000, seed 20261121) 95% interval; and F6 vs the R1 distribution (empirical p)

C2_leave_one_out.question: Hide one category of an order: do the rules guess it?
C2_leave_one_out.cases: every (order, category c) with the order's mapped l2 set S of size >= 2 ('other' dropped)
C2_leave_one_out.rules_used: the directed P5 rules whose combination is in the customer's group list at budget B (B = 100 primary, B = 20 secondary); score of a rule = its Discovery confidence in its own scope
C2_leave_one_out.prediction: context = S minus c; a rule fires if its antecedent is a subset of the context and its consequent is not in the context; each candidate consequent gets the maximum score of its fired rules; candidates are ranked by score desc, then by Discovery joint count desc, then by category index asc
C2_leave_one_out.hit_at_k: 1 if c is among the first k candidates; cases with no fired rule are misses; k = 3 primary, also 1 and 5
C2_leave_one_out.summary: mean hit over cases (case-weighted) and customer-macro mean
C2_leave_one_out.controls: to keep runtime bounded: F with A1 and B2 only, F6 with A1 and R1 only (100 seeds each)
C2_leave_one_out.primary: H2: F6 hit@3 at B=100 minus G, paired customer bootstrap interval; F6 vs R1

C3_worst_group.question: Does segmentation help the group that the global list serves worst?
C3_worst_group.metric: for a system with groups g: own(g) = coverage of g's Validation orders by g's own list, glob(g) = coverage of the same orders by G's list; g* = group with the lowest glob(g); worst_gain = own(g*) - glob(g*); equal_gain = unweighted mean over groups of own(g) - glob(g)
C3_worst_group.budgets: all five; summary over small budgets = mean of worst_gain over 5, 10, 20
C3_worst_group.primary: H3: F6 worst_gain small-budget mean vs the R1 distribution (empirical p); also its value

C4_revenue_weighted.question: If orders are weighted by money, are segmented lists better?
C4_revenue_weighted.metric: share of Validation gross_purchase_amount in covered orders (E9 lists), every budget; summary = mean over 5, 10, 20
C4_revenue_weighted.interval: paired customer bootstrap of the weighted share difference (same resampling as C1)
C4_revenue_weighted.primary: H4: F6 revenue-weighted small-budget mean minus G, interval; F6 vs R1

reading_rules.validation: descriptive only. A comparison 'looks favourable' if the F6 - G interval is above 0 (H1, H2, H4) or worst_gain > 0 (H3), AND F6 is above the R1 95th percentile (empirical p <= 0.05).
reading_rules.test_if_run: the same four statistics, Holm correction over H1-H4 on the empirical p versus R1; a hypothesis is supported only if its interval (H1, H2, H4) is above 0 / worst_gain > 0 (H3) AND its Holm-adjusted p <= 0.05. All four are reported whatever the outcome.
